# A combinatorial interpretation of Kronecker coefficients

<!-- Generated by MathResearchLab. This file is rewritten on every sync; edit the app, not this file. -->

**Status:** Open per source; openness not yet verified

## Statement

Original wording (verbatim from the source):

```latex
Stanley's Problem~10 asks for a combinatorial interpretation of these multiplicities.
```

Normalized:

Give an explicit family of finite combinatorial sets $\mathcal K(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ such that for every integer $n\geq1$ and every $\lambda,\mu,\nu\vdash n$, $|\mathcal K(\lambda,\mu,\nu)|=g_{\lambda,\mu,\nu}$.

Source: Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, Emily Xia Meng, Henry Kvinge, *PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models*, arXiv:2611.33966, p. 6, 4.2 Kronecker coefficients

## Definitions

- **Kronecker coefficient**: A partition $\lambda\vdash n$ indexes an irreducible complex representation $V^\lambda$ of $S_n$. The integer $g_{\lambda,\mu,\nu}$ is the multiplicity of $V^\nu$ in $V^\lambda\otimes V^\mu$.

## Known results

- A direct baseline gave a matching rule when one index is a two-row partition. Testing membership can require constructing large lists. *(Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models, arXiv:2611.33966 (Appendix C, Table 22, p. 46))*
- Positivity requires $n-\lambda_1,n-\mu_1,n-\nu_1$ to satisfy the triangle inequalities. The coefficient is at most two when two indices are hooks and at most three when two indices are a hook and a two-row partition. *(Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models, arXiv:2611.33966 (B.2.3, Theorems B.2.1–B.2.2, p. 29))*
